items.headline: Common Sense Media Releases New Research on Teens and AI-Generated Explicit Material
items.dek: SAN FRANCISCO, July 21, 2026—Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute today released new research that reveals some concerning truths about teens' use of AI to create explicit deepfakes. The report found that nearly half of teens have already seen AI-generated explicit sexual material, and almost a quarter have seen it depicting themselves or someone they know.

items.dek: "AI has made it possible for anyone, at any time, to create nude images and videos with one click," said Common Sense Media founder and CEO James P. Steyer. "Our new research confirms that, even if parents don't know it, many teens are seeing explicit deepfakes online. It's time for parents to start having honest, judgment-free conversations with their teens about AI and pornography. These talks aren't always easy, but they are always necessary."

items.dek: Researchers from Common Sense Media and the global communications firm Burson surveyed a demographically representative set of 1,314 teens age 13 to 17 in the United States. Key findings from the report include:
items.outlet: Common Sense Media (Youth AI Safety Institute)
items.caption: Methodology sentence (1,314 teens, Burson) + the 5 key-finding bullets of the press release
items.notes: 9 highlight boxes: sample; 67% fear; girls 71% vs boys 62%; 18% made/know; 25% shared; 63% people they know; boys 11% vs girls 4%; 82% illegal; 23% "no one gets hurt". w960 alt is more square (good for half-slide).

highlights.text: surveyed a demographically representative set of 1,314 teens age 13 to 17 in the United States
Two-thirds of teens (67%) fear being deepfaked without consent
Girls are more worried than boys (71% vs. 62%).
1 in 5 (18%) has made AI pornography or knows someone who has
25% have shared it or know someone who has
63% have created pornography depicting themselves or people they know
Boys are almost three times as likely as girls to have made it (11% vs. 4%).
82% who have seen AI-generated pornography say creating it without consent should be illegal
23% believe AI nudes are less harmful than real ones "because no one gets hurt."

Our nationally representative survey of 1,314 teens age 13 to 17, conducted in fall 2025,
nearly half of teens have seen AI-generated explicit material.

facts.claim: 8% of teens have personally made AI sexual content; boys are almost three times as likely as girls (11% vs 4%).
facts.verbatim: Boys are almost three times as likely as girls to have made it (11% vs. 4%).

facts.claim: Two-thirds of teens (67%) fear being deepfaked without consent; girls 71% vs boys 62%. Worried teens are making accounts private (30%), posting less (23%) or deleting accounts (9%).
facts.verbatim: Two-thirds of teens (67%) fear being deepfaked without consent, and many are scaling back online activity to protect themselves.

facts.claim: 82% of teens who have seen AI porn say creating it without consent should be illegal, yet 23% believe AI nudes are less harmful "because no one gets hurt."
facts.verbatim: 82% who have seen AI-generated pornography say creating it without consent should be illegal, but 23% believe AI nudes are less harmful than real ones "because no one gets hurt."

facts.claim: Only 20% of teens have discussed AI-generated sexual content with a trusted adult; 34% want to talk to an adult but don't know how to start.
facts.verbatim: Only 20% of teens have discussed AI-generated sexual content with a trusted adult, and a third want to but don't know how to start.

facts.claim: 19% of teens would not feel comfortable talking to anyone about disturbing AI sexual content; 10% would turn to an AI chatbot.
Roughly two-thirds of teens think AI sexual content shapes how peers think about what bodies should look like (66%), trust in media (65%) and expectations of romantic partners (64%).
Among teens who have seen AI sexual content, 82% encountered it on social media, incl. TikTok (33%), Instagram (27%) and X/Twitter (25%); 41% on porn sites.
facts.source: Common Sense Media (2026), Key Finding 2 & Figure E
facts.verbatim: The content shows up across platforms that teens use every day, including TikTok (33%), Instagram (27%), and X/Twitter (25%), among others.

facts.claim: 16% of teens who have seen AI sexual content encountered it on AI chatbot platforms ("ChatGPT, Grok, Claude, etc."); 15% via AI apps that make or modify photos/videos.
facts.verbatim: AI chatbot platforms (ChatGPT, Grok, Claude, etc.)

facts.claim: 74% of teens have seen online pornography (73% in 2023); 52% first saw it by age 12.
facts.verbatim: Seventy-four percent of teens report having seen online pornography. More than half (52%) first encountered it by age 12, including 12% by age 10 or younger.

facts.claim: "AI has made it possible for anyone, at any time, to create nude images and videos with one click." — James P. Steyer, Common Sense Media CEO
facts.verbatim: "AI has made it possible for anyone, at any time, to create nude images and videos with one click," said Common Sense Media founder and CEO James P. Steyer.

facts.claim: "With no hurdles or anything you have to jump over, you can just do it right there." — boy, 17 (Common Sense focus group)
facts.verbatim: "With no hurdles or anything you have to jump over, you can just do it right there." Boy, age 17

facts.claim: Survey methodology: nationally representative online survey of 1,314 U.S. teens aged 13-17 by Common Sense Media and Burson; 12-minute survey fielded Nov 21-Dec 9, 2025; weighted to Census; margin of error ±2.7 points; plus 20 interviews (Sept 22-Oct 21, 2025) and 2 focus groups (Feb 25-26, 2026).
facts.verbatim: Data collection was conducted from November 21, 2025, to December 9, 2025.

facts.claim: AI-generated sexual content of anyone under 18 is felony-level child sexual abuse material (CSAM).
facts.verbatim: It is important to note that AI-generated sexual content of youth under 18 is considered felony-level child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

facts.claim: CDT: 12% of high school students have heard of deepfake nonconsensual sexual images depicting someone associated with their school (2024-25 school year).
facts.source: Common Sense Media (2026) Introduction, citing CDT (Laird et al., 2025)
facts.verbatim: According to the Center for Democracy and Technology, 12% of high school students have heard of deepfake nonconsensual sexual images being shared that depict someone associated with their school (Laird et al., 2025).

facts.claim: CDT 2025: only 40% of students got any guidance on deepfake NCII and just 11% were told where to report it; 21% of teachers say their school shared deepfake-NCII policies.
facts.source: Benton Institute summary of CDT "Hand in Hand" (Oct 2, 2025)
facts.verbatim: Less than half of students (40 percent) reported receiving guidance or discussion on deepfake NCII, and just 11 percent had been told where to report it.

facts.claim: Thorn 2026: 4% of U.S. teens say deepfake nudes have been made of them (1 in 25); 7% have seen a deepfake nude of another kid; 13% aren't sure; 2% have made one.
facts.source: Thorn, Youth Perspectives on Online Safety, 2025 (July 2026)
facts.verbatim: Among teens surveyed, 4% reported having had a personal experience with deepfake nudes being created of them, and 7% reported having seen a deepfake nude of another kid or teen.

facts.claim: Thorn 2026: 67% of minors (9-17) have used an AI chatbot or companion; after an online sexual interaction, 15% sought guidance from an AI chatbot — twice the rate for bullying (7%).
facts.verbatim: 67% of minors surveyed have reported using an AI chatbot or companion.

facts.claim: Thorn 2026: counting SG-CSAM, sextortion and deepfake-nude experiences, nearly 1 in 2 teens (45%) reported at least one type of sexual interaction online.
facts.verbatim: nearly 1 in 2 teens (45%) reported having at least one type of sexual interaction online.

facts.claim: Thorn survey methodology: 1,003 U.S. minors aged 9-17, 18-minute online survey, Nov 12-Dec 1, 2025, with Burson; weighted to Census; deepfake questions asked of teens 13-17 only.
facts.verbatim: In total, 1,003 minors from across the United States participated in an 18-minute online survey between November 12 and December 1, 2025.

facts.claim: NCMEC: GAI-related CyberTipline reports rose from 4,700 (2023) to 67,000 (2024) to more than 400,000 (2025).
facts.verbatim: More than 400,000 CyberTipline reports of GAI from the public and ESPs

facts.claim: NCMEC: in 2025 more than 182,000 CyberTipline reports involved offenders possessing, generating or attempting to generate AI-generated CSAM.
facts.verbatim: more than 182,000 reports involved offenders possessing, generating or attempting to generate GAI CSAM

facts.claim: NCMEC: since 2023, more than 275 victims of AI-generated CSAM identified and more than 158,000 images and videos categorized as AI CSAM; offenders were often people in the child's life.
facts.verbatim: Since 2023, when we started tracking the use of GAI, more than 275 victims of GAI CSAM have been identified, and more than 158,000 images and videos have been categorized as GAI CSAM.

facts.claim: NCMEC: companies (ESPs) flagged just over 11,000 images/videos as AI-generated (Jan 2023-Dec 2025) vs. 158,000+ categorized by NCMEC staff.
NCMEC: CyberTipline received 21.3 million reports in 2025 (61.8 million files).
facts.verbatim: In 2025, the CyberTipline received 21.3 million reports

facts.claim: NCMEC (Aug 2026): nudify-app incidents are growing in schools nationwide, most often involving classmates ages 14 to 17.
facts.verbatim: NCMEC is seeing a growing number of these incidents in schools across the country, most often involving classmates ages 14 to 17.

facts.claim: RAND: 13% of U.S. principals reported deepfake bullying incidents in 2023-24/2024-25 — 22% of high schools and 20% of middle schools.
facts.verbatim: we found that 13 percent of principals reported incidents of bullying that involved AI-generated deepfakes during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 school years

Thorn's 2026 deepfake data are inside "Youth Perspectives on Online Safety, 2025" (published July 2026). Thorn's dedicated "Deepfake Nudes & Young People" report is from March 2025 (already in manifest as thorn-teens-deepfake-stat). Note the 2026 victim rate (4%) is lower than the 2025 report's 6% (1 in 17) — different samples.

caveats: Common Sense Youth AI Safety Institute discloses it "is funded by both philanthropy and industry, including the makers of some of the technologies it evaluates" (press release About section); the report itself lists Oak Foundation as funder.
Date wording differs: landing page says survey "conducted in fall 2025"; methodology gives survey fieldwork Nov 21-Dec 9, 2025 and overall data collection Sept 22, 2025-Feb 26, 2026.
Press release says "1 in 5 (18%) has made AI pornography or knows someone who has" — 18% is the combined made-or-know figure; only 8% made it themselves.
24%/"almost a quarter" is among teens who have SEEN AI sexual content (n=586), not all teens; the 82% and 23% figures are also among those who have seen it.
NCMEC GAI page says 275 direct victims "identified in 2024 and 2025 alone"; the 2025 CyberTipline Report says "Since 2023" — use "more than 275 since tracking began" to be safe.
